URL: https://ait.ac.th/study/flexible-masters-option/

# Flexible Master’s Option

The “Flexible Master’s Option” is a new alternative to our traditional “On-campus Master Option” to conduct Master studies at AIT. It is applicable to selected programs at all of our schools. Students will receive the same degree and the same academic requirements apply as the program offered in our regular “On-campus Option”. Students can do almost all coursework online via AIT’s Hybrid Mode of Instruction (certain programs may require a lab and research work on campus).

## How it Works

Typically, the 1st year is online via AIT’s Hybrid Instruction. Students may spread coursework over more than one year. Students take the same course offered to on-campus students via Hybrid Mode. All classes are recorded for later viewing.

After completion of the coursework, students can do their research or thesis in the AIT Campus at a flexible time.

The application is currently open.

## Payment

First, you need to decide for how many courses you want to enrollee, the minimum enrollment is 6 credits which is equivalent to 2 courses. The Program Secretary can advise you on details. You need to pay the full fee for your courses before the start of the semester.All details to make payments are at this website,Click here.

## Contact & Support

For More Inquiry, please contact:admissions@ait.ac.th

# Flexible Master’s Option

The “Flexible Master’s Option” is a new alternative to our traditional “On-campus Master Option” to conduct Master studies at AIT. It is applicable to selected programs at all of our schools. Students will receive the same degree and the same academic requirements apply as the program offered in our regular “On-campus Option”. Students can do almost all coursework online via AIT’s Hybrid Mode of Instruction (certain programs may require a lab and research work on campus).

## How it Works

Typically, the 1st year is online via AIT’s Hybrid Instruction. Students may spread coursework over more than one year. Students take the same course offered to on-campus students via Hybrid Mode. All classes are recorded for later viewing.

After completion of the coursework, students can do their research or thesis in the AIT Campus at a flexible time.

# Agri-Business Management (ABM)
Agriculture plays a vital role in the economic development of a majority of developing countries. Moreover, agriculture is the provider of food and feed to the world. The agro-industries are also contributing to the growing industrialization of developing countries leading to the increasing importance of agri-products. The development of agribusinesses is also influenced by trade policies. Thus, the management of agribusinesses requires a holistic skill set to navigate challenges posed by the inherently unpredictable nature of agricultural products and government policies. ## Introduction / Background

The Development Innovation and Sustainability (DIS) academic program is a consolidated and forward-looking initiative of the Asian Institute of Technology (AIT), developed in response to increasingly complex development challenges in Asia and beyond. It integrates the strengths of two established programs—Development Planning, Management and Innovation (DPMI) and Development and Sustainability (DS)—into a coherent, interdisciplinary, and practice-oriented program aligned with the SDGs and the people–planet–prosperity nexus. ### A Legacy of Impact

As sustainability and social equity become more critical than ever, AIT continues to champion innovation and inclusivity in its journey toward a greener, fairer, and more resilient future.

# Doctoral Degree Program

To be eligible for admission to the regular Doctoral degree program, an applicant must:

* Have strong academic records (both undergraduate and graduate) and normally hold a four-year bachelor’s degree and a Master’s degree*, preferably with a combination of course and thesis work, from an institution of good standing, acceptable to AIT. * Submit a brief outline of dissertation research proposal (5-10 pages) including the required research facilities, if necessary.
* Two recommendation letters.

# Engineering  Entrepreneurship

### Become an Engineer Entrepreneur, Join our Engineering Entrepreneurship Program.

### ABOUT THE PROGRAM

The Engineering Entrepreneurship Program combines advanced engineering knowledge with entrepreneurial skills and mindset. Choose any engineering discipline in our School of Engineering and Technology (SET) and add our Entrepreneurship Minor. Get two major skills in one program.

* Learn advanced engineering knowledge
* Learn how to start your own business

# Food Innovation, Bioprocessing, Nutrition and Health (FIBNH)

## Introduction / Background

The region’s growing industrial sector and the increasing demand for high technologies have brought the need for expertise in Semiconductor to a critical level. The Master Program in Semiconductor, introduced in May 2000, responds to the needs of countries in Southeast Asia, many of which are in transition from labor-intensive to high-tech industries. The curriculum focuses on the design and IC packaging aspects for specific applications. Fabrication, including prototyping of chips, is included in the curriculum and is featured in partnership with Semiconductor industries and collaborating universities overseas. Currently, courses in Bio-Nano Materials Science and Engineering are being added to the offerings of the field.

# Transportation Engineering (TRE)

## Introduction

Industrialization and population growth have tremendous impacts on the movement of people and goods. Every day, movement is hampered by congestion, insufficiency of public transport facilities, traffic accidents, and other conditions. Moreover, as manufacturing expands globally, businesses want to reduce transportation costs by limiting the number of distribution nodes. Concerns over congestion on highways, increasing pollution and hazardous materials all emphasize the need to effectively maximize transportation systems. Thus, the issue of transportation is obviously crucial, not only now but in the future.

TheTransportation Engineeringfield exposes students to the process of alleviating transportation problems. The coursework and research in the area provide advanced knowledge in transportation pl

electives from other fields/schools as part of an approved study plan.

## Course Structure

Master’s Program

A master’s program requires 48 credits with two options:

Yet, many regions, particularly developing nations, continue to struggle with floods, droughts, pollution, and competing sectoral demands. These challenges are further amplified in Asia, the world’s most populous and climate-vulnerable region, where effective water management will directly determine economic growth, human well-being, and ecological integrity.

The Water Engineering and Management (WEM) program at AIT aims to address these contemporary challenges in water resources and its sustainable development and management. For an overseas applicant applying for the **January intake** at **AIT (Assumption University)** and requiring an **educational visa**, the relevant deadlines and guidelines are as follows:

### **Key Deadlines for January Intake**
1. **General Deadline for Overseas Applicants (Educational Visa):**  
   - **20 December** is the deadline for overseas applicants requiring an educational visa for the **January Semester/Term Intake** (as stated in sources [2] and [3]).  
   - However, some sources (e.g., [4][7]) mention **30 June** as the deadline for overseas applicants needing an educational visa for the **August Semester/Term Intake** (which corresponds to the January academic year start). This discrepancy may arise from differing interpretations of "January intake" (e.g., whether it refers to the academic term starting in January or the application cycle for that term).  

   **Clarification:**  
   - If the January intake refers to the **academic term starting in January**, the **20 December** deadline applies.  
   - If the January intake refers to the **August application cycle** (common in Thai universities), the **30 June** deadline applies.  
   - Always confirm with AIT’s admissions team to resolve ambiguity.

---

### **Educational Visa Requirements**
1. **Visa Type:**  
   - Apply for a **non-immigrant visa (ED plus)** for degree programs.  
   - For exchange or visiting students, apply for **ED** visa (special programs).  
   - **Avoid tourist visas (T)**, as they will result in immediate deportation.  

2. **Documents Required:**  
   - AIT’s **visa request letter** and **Certificate of Admission**.  
   - Passport with valid visa (ED/ED plus).  
   - Additional documents may be requested by Thai embassies (e.g., proof of funds, academic transcripts).  

3. **Application Process:**  
   - Submit the visa application to the **Thai Embassy/Consulate** promptly.  
   - Ensure the visa is valid before arriving in Thailand.  

---

### **Scholarship Deadlines (Relevant for Visa Applicants)**
- **30 June** is the deadline for overseas applicants requiring an educational visa for **AIT Scholarships** (including RTG Fellowships) under the August Semester/Term Intake (January intake).  
- Other scholarships (e.g., HM King’s/Queen’s, GMS, ADB-JSP) have earlier deadlines (e.g., 31 March).  

---

### **Important Notes**
- **Conflicting Deadlines:** Some sources list **20 December** for January intake, while others list **30 June** for August Semester/Term Intake. This may depend on the specific faculty or program. Verify with AIT’s admissions office.  
- **Visa Application:** Always apply for the correct visa type (ED/ED plus) and ensure all documents are submitted well in advance.  

For further details, refer to AIT’s official guidelines: [AIT Visa Guidelines](https://ait.ac.th/guidelines-for-applicants-who-were-offered-admission/).

generation.answer_text:
For an overseas applicant applying for the **January intake** at **AIT (Assumption University)** and requiring an **educational visa**, the relevant deadlines and guidelines are as follows:

### **Key Deadlines for January Intake**
1. **General Deadline for Overseas Applicants (Educational Visa):**  
   - **20 December** is the deadline for overseas applicants requiring an educational visa for the **January Semester/Term Intake** (as stated in sources [2] and [3]).  
   - However, some sources (e.g., [4][7]) mention **30 June** as the deadline for overseas applicants needing an educational visa for the **August Semester/Term Intake** (which corresponds to the January academic year start). This discrepancy may arise from differing interpretations of "January intake" (e.g., whether it refers to the academic term starting in January or the application cycle for that term).  

   **Clarification:**  
   - If the January intake refers to the **academic term starting in January**, the **20 December** deadline applies.  
   - If the January intake refers to the **August application cycle** (common in Thai universities), the **30 June** deadline applies.  
   - Always confirm with AIT’s admissions team to resolve ambiguity.

---

### **Educational Visa Requirements**
1. **Visa Type:**  
   - Apply for a **non-immigrant visa (ED plus)** for degree programs.  
   - For exchange or visiting students, apply for **ED** visa (special programs).  
   - **Avoid tourist visas (T)**, as they will result in immediate deportation.  

2. **Documents Required:**  
   - AIT’s **visa request letter** and **Certificate of Admission**.  
   - Passport with valid visa (ED/ED plus).  
   - Additional documents may be requested by Thai embassies (e.g., proof of funds, academic transcripts).  

3. **Application Process:**  
   - Submit the visa application to the **Thai Embassy/Consulate** promptly.  
   - Ensure the visa is valid before arriving in Thailand.  

---

### **Scholarship Deadlines (Relevant for Visa Applicants)**
- **30 June** is the deadline for overseas applicants requiring an educational visa for **AIT Scholarships** (including RTG Fellowships) under the August Semester/Term Intake (January intake).  
- Other scholarships (e.g., HM King’s/Queen’s, GMS, ADB-JSP) have earlier deadlines (e.g., 31 March).  

---

### **Important Notes**
- **Conflicting Deadlines:** Some sources list **20 December** for January intake, while others list **30 June** for August Semester/Term Intake. This may depend on the specific faculty or program. Verify with AIT’s admissions office.  
- **Visa Application:** Always apply for the correct visa type (ED/ED plus) and ensure all documents are submitted well in advance.  

For further details, refer to AIT’s official guidelines: [AIT Visa Guidelines](https://ait.ac.th/guidelines-for-applicants-who-were-offered-admission/).

generation.answer_text:
For an overseas applicant applying for the **January intake** at **AIT (Assumption University)** and requiring an **educational visa**, the relevant deadlines and guidelines are as follows:

### **Key Deadlines for January Intake**
1. **General Deadline for Overseas Applicants (Educational Visa):**  
   - **20 December** is the deadline for overseas applicants requiring an educational visa for the **January Semester/Term Intake** (as stated in sources [2] and [3]).  
   - However, some sources (e.g., [4][7]) mention **30 June** as the deadline for overseas applicants needing an educational visa for the **August Semester/Term Intake** (which corresponds to the January academic year start). This discrepancy may arise from differing interpretations of "January intake" (e.g., whether it refers to the academic term starting in January or the application cycle for that term).  

   **Clarification:**  
   - If the January intake refers to the **academic term starting in January**, the **20 December** deadline applies.  
   - If the January intake refers to the **August application cycle** (common in Thai universities), the **30 June** deadline applies.  
   - Always confirm with AIT’s admissions team to resolve ambiguity.

---

### **Educational Visa Requirements**
1. **Visa Type:**  
   - Apply for a **non-immigrant visa (ED plus)** for degree programs.  
   - For exchange or visiting students, apply for **ED** visa (special programs).  
   - **Avoid tourist visas (T)**, as they will result in immediate deportation.  

2. **Documents Required:**  
   - AIT’s **visa request letter** and **Certificate of Admission**.  
   - Passport with valid visa (ED/ED plus).  
   - Additional documents may be requested by Thai embassies (e.g., proof of funds, academic transcripts).  

3. **Application Process:**  
   - Submit the visa application to the **Thai Embassy/Consulate** promptly.  
   - Ensure the visa is valid before arriving in Thailand.  

---

### **Scholarship Deadlines (Relevant for Visa Applicants)**
- **30 June** is the deadline for overseas applicants requiring an educational visa for **AIT Scholarships** (including RTG Fellowships) under the August Semester/Term Intake (January intake).  
- Other scholarships (e.g., HM King’s/Queen’s, GMS, ADB-JSP) have earlier deadlines (e.g., 31 March).  

---

### **Important Notes**
- **Conflicting Deadlines:** Some sources list **20 December** for January intake, while others list **30 June** for August Semester/Term Intake. This may depend on the specific faculty or program. Verify with AIT’s admissions office.  
- **Visa Application:** Always apply for the correct visa type (ED/ED plus) and ensure all documents are submitted well in advance.  

For further details, refer to AIT’s official guidelines: [AIT Visa Guidelines](https://ait.ac.th/guidelines-for-applicants-who-were-offered-admission/).

- Hold a four-year bachelor’s degree and a Master’s degree (preferably with course and thesis work) from an institution of good standing, with a minimum CGPA of 3.50 or equivalent at the Master’s level.  
- Meet English proficiency requirements (AIT-EET: 6; IELTS Academic: overall 6 [writing 6]; TOEFL iBT: overall 80 [writing 21-23]; PTE Academic: overall 52 [writing 62-73]).  
- Submit a brief dissertation research proposal (5–10 pages) including required research facilities.  
- Provide two recommendation letters.  

Applicants with a one-year master’s degree, a one-year professional master’s degree, or a one-year postgraduate diploma may enroll in the doctoral program by completing an additional 12–24 credits of coursework, achieving a CGPA of 3.5, and obtaining a very good or excellent grade in their research study, in addition to the required 84 credits for the doctoral program.  

The doctoral program requires a minimum of 84 credits, comprising 12 credits of coursework at AIT (including 3 credits of special study) and 72 credits for the dissertation.  

For more details, visit [AIT’s doctoral program page](https://ait.ac.th/eligibility/doctoral-degree-program/).

* If outstanding amount exceeds two-months rental, student will be required to vacate the rooms.

Yes, on-campus accommodation is available at AIT. The campus accommodation includes both air-conditioned and non-air-conditioned rooms, with 53% of units having cooking facilities. All rooms are fully furnished and include regular maintenance services, weekly cleaning, and linens (one set per student, including one pillowcase, two bedsheets, and one pillow).

For new students, accommodation is allocated upon arrival through a lottery system. Continuing students must register to queue for their preferred room type at the accommodation office.
